title: CHEAR: Confusion-Hierarchy Evidence-Aware Reasoning for Cost-Efficient Human Activity Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2610.15298v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer a new approach to wearable-sensor-based human activity recognition. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further introduces similar motion examples and discriminative sensor knowledge, enabling decisions grounded in observations relevant to the current query. More evidence, however, does not necessarily mean better-organized evidence. When online prompts and LLM agents primarily orchestrate inference, decisions about which activities to compare and when to invoke discriminative knowledge remain concentrated at inference time. As the activity vocabulary grows, the model must repeatedly process more candidates and associated knowledge, whereas pruning candidates too early risks excluding the true activity. translated_title: CHEAR：面向高性价比人体活动识别的混淆层次证据感知推理
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）为基于可穿戴传感器的人体活动识别提供了一种新方法。检索增强生成（RAG）进一步引入相似的运动示例和判别性传感器知识，使决策能够基于与当前查询相关的观测结果进行。然而，证据更多并不一定意味着证据组织得更好。当在线提示与LLM智能体主要承担推理编排时，关于比较哪些活动以及何时调用判别知识的决策仍然集中在推理阶段。随着活动词汇规模的扩大，模型必须反复处理更多的候选活动及其相关知识，而过早剪枝候选活动又可能将真正的活动排除在外。我们提出混淆层次证据感知推理（CHEAR），将部分知识组织工作转移到离线完成。CHEAR从跨被试的复发性混淆中构建并验证一个活动层次结构……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: CHEAR将活动比较与判别知识的组织工作从推理阶段转移到离线阶段，通过从跨被试混淆中构建并验证活动层次结构，实现随活动词汇增长仍保持低成本的人体活动识别。
en_tdlr: CHEAR shifts knowledge organization offline by constructing and validating an activity hierarchy from cross-subject confusions, enabling cost-efficient LLM-based human activity recognition as the activity vocabulary grows.
